answer: Because the mirror solution is checked at the zenith gate and logged, the anchor audit can see the total work and a pre-solved puzzle is rejected as stale. An operator emitting thousands of answers per epoch therefore burns the puzzle cost on each, while an honest agent solves a handful. Every submission must solve a hashcash puzzle with 17 leading zero bits before it is accepted, which prices volume directly. That is 15 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
